# GRC_Claw Data Storage Specification

**Version:** 1.1  
**Date:** 2026-10-01  
**Status:** Draft  
**Owner:** GRC_Claw Architecture Team

---

## 1. Purpose & Scope

This specification defines how GRC_Claw stores, secures, and maintains all governance data. It covers the five core data models, four storage backends, retention policies, encryption standards, backup/recovery procedures, data lifecycle automation, storage tiering, compression and deduplication, performance optimization, multi-region replication, and storage cost optimization.

**In scope:** All persistent data generated by or ingested into GRC_Claw — policies, evidence, enforcement actions, assessments, and compliance records.

**Out of scope:** Application-layer caching, in-memory session state, and third-party SaaS configurations.

---

## 2. Architecture Overview

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    GRC_Claw Application                  │
├──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬────────────────────────┤
│ Policy   │ Evidence │Enforcement│ Assessment │ Compliance│
│ Service  │ Service  │ Service   │ Service   │ Service   │
├──────────┴──────────┴──────────┴────────────────────────┤
│              Storage Abstraction Layer                   │
├──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬────────────────────────┤
│Relational│ Document │  Graph   │    Time-Series         │
│PostgreSQL│MongoDB   │Neo4j     │    TimescaleDB         │
└──────────┴──────────┴──────────┴────────────────────────┘
```

Each data model is assigned a **primary** backend and may use **secondary** backends for specific access patterns.

---

## 3. Data Models

### 3.1 Policy Model

**Primary Backend:** PostgreSQL (relational)  
**Secondary Backend:** MongoDB (document, for versioned policy text)

#### Schema (PostgreSQL)

```sql
CREATE TABLE policies (
    id              UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    policy_key      VARCHAR(128) UNIQUE NOT NULL,    -- e.g., "AI-ETHICS-001"
    title           VARCHAR(512) NOT NULL,
    description     TEXT,
    category        VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,            -- ethics, safety, privacy, fairness
    status          VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft',  -- draft, active, deprecated, archived
    version         INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
    effective_date  TIMESTAMPTZ,
    expiry_date     TIMESTAMPTZ,
    owner_id        UUID NOT NULL,                   -- references users table
    metadata        JSONB,                            -- flexible key-value store
    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    created_by      UUID NOT NULL,
    updated_by      UUID NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE policy_clauses (
    id              UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    policy_id       UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES policies(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    clause_number   VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL,            -- e.g., "3.2.a"
    title           VARCHAR(256) NOT NULL,
    body            TEXT NOT NULL,
    severity        VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'medium',  -- critical, high, medium, low
    enforcement_type VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL,            -- automated, manual, hybrid
    metadata        JSONB,
    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE TABLE policy_relationships (
    id              UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    source_policy   UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES policies(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    target_policy   UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES policies(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    relation_type   VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,            -- supersedes, conflicts_with, derives_from, related_to
    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    UNIQUE(source_policy, target_policy, relation_type)
);

CREATE INDEX idx_policies_category ON policies(category);
CREATE INDEX idx_policies_status ON policies(status);
CREATE INDEX idx_policies_effective ON policies(effective_date, expiry_date);
CREATE INDEX idx_policy_clauses_policy ON policy_clauses(policy_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_policy_rel_source ON policy_relationships(source_policy);
CREATE INDEX idx_policy_rel_target ON policy_relationships(target_policy);
```

#### Document Store (MongoDB)

```json
// Collection: policy_versions
{
  "_id": "ObjectId",
  "policy_id": "UUID (matches PostgreSQL)",
  "version": 3,
  "full_text": "Markdown-rendered complete policy document",
  "change_summary": "Added clause 3.4 on data minimization",
  "diff_from_previous": "Unified diff format",
  "approved_by": "UUID",
  "approved_at": "ISODate",
  "created_at": "ISODate"
}
```

**Rationale:** PostgreSQL enforces referential integrity for policy metadata and relationships. MongoDB stores versioned full-text documents for audit and rendering purposes.

### 3.2 Evidence Model

**Primary Backend:** MongoDB (document)  
**Secondary Backend:** TimescaleDB (time-series, for metrics-based evidence)

#### Schema (MongoDB)

```json
// Collection: evidence
{
  "_id": "ObjectId",
  "evidence_id": "UUID",
  "policy_id": "UUID (references policies.id)",
  "assessment_id": "UUID (optional, references assessments)",
  "source": {
    "type": "scan|audit|manual|api|log",
    "system": "string",
    "collection_method": "string"
  },
  "evidence_type": "config|log|metric|screenshot|report|attestation",
  "content": {
    "format": "json|text|binary|image",
    "data": "mixed",
    "hash": "SHA-256 of raw content"
  },
  "context": {
    "environment": "prod|staging|dev",
    "region": "string",
    "timestamp": "ISODate",
    "metadata": {}
  },
  "validation": {
    "status": "pending|validated|rejected|expired",
    "validated_by": "UUID",
    "validated_at": "ISODate",
    "confidence_score": 0.0
  },
  "retention_class": "standard|extended|permanent",
  "created_at": "ISODate",
  "expires_at": "ISODate"
}
```

#### Time-Series Schema (TimescaleDB)

```sql
CREATE TABLE evidence_metrics (
    time            TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    evidence_id     UUID NOT NULL,
    policy_id       UUID NOT NULL,
    metric_name     VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL,
    metric_value    DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL,
    unit            VARCHAR(32),
    labels          JSONB,
    source          VARCHAR(128)
);

SELECT create_hypertable('evidence_metrics', 'time');

CREATE INDEX idx_evidence_metrics_policy ON evidence_metrics(policy_id, time DESC);
CREATE INDEX idx_evidence_metrics_name ON evidence_metrics(metric_name, time DESC);
```

**Rationale:** Evidence is inherently heterogeneous — documents, logs, metrics, screenshots. MongoDB's flexible schema accommodates this. Time-series metrics (e.g., model drift measurements, latency percentiles) go to TimescaleDB for efficient aggregation.

### 3.3 Enforcement Model

**Primary Backend:** PostgreSQL (relational)  
**Secondary Backend:** Neo4j (graph, for dependency tracking)

#### Schema (PostgreSQL)

```sql
CREATE TABLE enforcement_actions (
    id              UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    action_key      VARCHAR(128) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
    policy_id       UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES policies(id),
    clause_id       UUID REFERENCES policy_clauses(id),
    evidence_id     UUID,                             -- triggers from evidence
    action_type     VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,            -- block, flag, quarantine, notify, escalate, auto_remediate
    target_type     VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,            -- model, dataset, endpoint, user, pipeline
    target_id       VARCHAR(256) NOT NULL,
    status          VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending',  -- pending, in_progress, completed, failed, rolled_back
    priority        VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'medium',  -- critical, high, medium, low
    triggered_by    UUID NOT NULL,                   -- user or system
    triggered_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    executed_at     TIMESTAMPTZ,
    completed_at    TIMESTAMPTZ,
    result          JSONB,                            -- execution result details
    error_message   TEXT,
    rollback_action JSONB,                            -- how to undo if needed
    metadata        JSONB,
    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE TABLE enforcement_audit_log (
    id              UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    action_id       UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES enforcement_actions(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    event_type      VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,            -- created, started, completed, failed, rolled_back
    event_data      JSONB,
    actor           UUID NOT NULL,
    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE INDEX idx_enforcement_policy ON enforcement_actions(policy_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_enforcement_status ON enforcement_actions(status);
CREATE INDEX idx_enforcement_target ON enforcement_actions(target_type, target_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_enforcement_triggered ON enforcement_actions(triggered_at);
CREATE INDEX idx_enforcement_audit_action ON enforcement_audit_log(action_id);
```

#### Graph Model (Neo4j)

```cypher
// Nodes
(:EnforcementAction {id, action_key, action_type, status, priority})
(:Policy {id, policy_key, title})
(:Target {id, target_type, target_id})
(:Evidence {id, evidence_id})

// Relationships
(:EnforcementAction)-[:ENFORCES]->(:Policy)
(:EnforcementAction)-[:TARGETS]->(:Target)
(:EnforcementAction)-[:TRIGGERED_BY]->(:Evidence)
(:EnforcementAction)-[:DEPENDS_ON]->(:EnforcementAction)  // for chained actions
(:EnforcementAction)-[:SUPERSEDED_BY]->(:EnforcementAction)
```

**Rationale:** Enforcement actions have strict state transitions and audit requirements — PostgreSQL's ACID guarantees are essential. Neo4j tracks action dependencies and blast radius (e.g., "if this model is blocked, which pipelines are affected?").

### 3.4 Assessment Model

**Primary Backend:** PostgreSQL (relational)  
**Secondary Backend:** MongoDB (document, for assessment reports)

#### Schema (PostgreSQL)

```sql
CREATE TABLE assessments (
    id              UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    assessment_key  VARCHAR(128) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
    title           VARCHAR(512) NOT NULL,
    description     TEXT,
    assessment_type VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,            -- risk, compliance, maturity, readiness
    target_id       VARCHAR(256) NOT NULL,           -- what is being assessed
    target_type     VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,            -- model, system, organization, process
    status          VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'planned',  -- planned, in_progress, completed, cancelled
    methodology     VARCHAR(128),                    -- e.g., "NIST AI RMF", "ISO 42001"
    score           NUMERIC(5,2),                    -- 0.00 - 100.00
    risk_level      VARCHAR(16),                     -- critical, high, medium, low
    started_at      TIMESTAMPTZ,
    completed_at    TIMESTAMPTZ,
    next_assessment_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
    lead_assessor   UUID NOT NULL,
    metadata        JSONB,
    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    created_by      UUID NOT NULL,
    updated_by      UUID NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE assessment_findings (
    id              UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    assessment_id   UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES assessments(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    finding_key     VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL,
    title           VARCHAR(512) NOT NULL,
    description     TEXT NOT NULL,
    severity        VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL,            -- critical, high, medium, low, informational
    category        VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    status          VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'open',  -- open, in_progress, resolved, accepted, false_positive
    policy_id       UUID REFERENCES policies(id),
    evidence_ids    UUID[],                          -- array of evidence UUIDs
    remediation    TEXT,
    remediated_by   UUID,
    remediated_at   TIMESTAMPTZ,
    due_date        TIMESTAMPTZ,
    metadata        JSONB,
    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE TABLE assessment_evidence_links (
    id              UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    assessment_id   UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES assessments(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    evidence_id     UUID NOT NULL,
    finding_id      UUID REFERENCES assessment_findings(id),
    relevance_score NUMERIC(3,2),                    -- 0.00 - 1.00
    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    UNIQUE(assessment_id, evidence_id, finding_id)
);

CREATE INDEX idx_assessments_type ON assessments(assessment_type);
CREATE INDEX idx_assessments_status ON assessments(status);
CREATE INDEX idx_assessments_target ON assessments(target_type, target_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_findings_assessment ON assessment_findings(assessment_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_findings_status ON assessment_findings(status);
CREATE INDEX idx_findings_severity ON assessment_findings(severity);
```

#### Document Store (MongoDB)

```json
// Collection: assessment_reports
{
  "_id": "ObjectId",
  "assessment_id": "UUID (matches PostgreSQL)",
  "report_format": "pdf|html|markdown",
  "full_report": "Base64-encoded or GridFS reference",
  "executive_summary": "string",
  "detailed_findings": [],
  "recommendations": [],
  "appendices": [],
  "generated_at": "ISODate",
  "generated_by": "UUID"
}
```

**Rationale:** Assessments have structured metadata (scores, dates, status) that benefit from relational integrity. Full assessment reports are large documents better suited to MongoDB/GridFS.

### 3.5 Compliance Model

**Primary Backend:** PostgreSQL (relational)  
**Secondary Backend:** Neo4j (graph, for compliance mapping)

#### Schema (PostgreSQL)

```sql
CREATE TABLE compliance_frameworks (
    id              UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    framework_key   VARCHAR(128) UNIQUE NOT NULL,    -- e.g., "NIST-AI-RMF", "ISO-42001", "EU-AI-ACT"
    name            VARCHAR(256) NOT NULL,
    version         VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    description     TEXT,
    authority       VARCHAR(256),                    -- issuing body
    effective_date  DATE,
    metadata        JSONB,
    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE TABLE compliance_controls (
    id              UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    framework_id    UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES compliance_frameworks(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    control_key     VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL,           -- e.g., "NIST-AI-RMF.GOVERN.1"
    title           VARCHAR(512) NOT NULL,
    description     TEXT NOT NULL,
    category        VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL,
    guidance        TEXT,                            -- implementation guidance
    metadata        JSONB,
    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    UNIQUE(framework_id, control_key)
);

CREATE TABLE compliance_mappings (
    id              UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    control_id      UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES compliance_controls(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    policy_id       UUID REFERENCES policies(id),
    assessment_id   UUID REFERENCES assessments(id),
    mapping_type    VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,            -- policy_satisfies, assessment_covers, evidence_supports
    coverage        VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'partial',  -- full, partial, none
    notes           TEXT,
    mapped_by       UUID NOT NULL,
    mapped_at       TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE TABLE compliance_status (
    id              UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    framework_id    UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES compliance_frameworks(id),
    control_id      UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES compliance_controls(id),
    target_id       VARCHAR(256) NOT NULL,           -- entity being evaluated
    target_type     VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    status          VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'unknown',  -- compliant, non_compliant, partial, not_assessed, exempt
    evidence_ids    UUID[],
    assessment_id   UUID REFERENCES assessments(id),
    evaluated_at    TIMESTAMPTZ,
    evaluated_by    UUID,
    next_review_at  TIMESTAMPTZ,
    notes           TEXT,
    metadata        JSONB,
    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    UNIQUE(framework_id, control_id, target_id, target_type)
);

CREATE TABLE compliance_attestations (
    id              UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    compliance_status_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES compliance_status(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    attestation_type VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,           -- self, internal_audit, external_audit, certification
    attested_by     UUID NOT NULL,
    attested_at     TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    valid_from      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    valid_until     TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    evidence_id     UUID,
    notes           TEXT,
    metadata        JSONB,
    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE INDEX idx_compliance_controls_framework ON compliance_controls(framework_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_compliance_mappings_control ON compliance_mappings(control_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_compliance_mappings_policy ON compliance_mappings(policy_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_compliance_status_framework ON compliance_status(framework_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_compliance_status_target ON compliance_status(target_type, target_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_compliance_status_review ON compliance_status(next_review_at);
CREATE INDEX idx_compliance_attestations_status ON compliance_attestations(compliance_status_id);
```

#### Graph Model (Neo4j)

```cypher
// Nodes
(:ComplianceFramework {id, framework_key, name})
(:ComplianceControl {id, control_key, title})
(:Policy {id, policy_key})
(:Assessment {id, assessment_key})
(:ComplianceStatus {id, status})

// Relationships
(:ComplianceFramework)-[:CONTAINS]->(:ComplianceControl)
(:ComplianceControl)-[:SATISFIED_BY {coverage}]->(:Policy)
(:ComplianceControl)-[:ASSESSED_BY]->(:Assessment)
(:ComplianceControl)-[:HAS_STATUS]->(:ComplianceStatus)
(:Policy)-[:MAPS_TO]->(:ComplianceControl)
```

**Rationale:** Compliance requires traceability from framework controls through policies to evidence. PostgreSQL stores the transactional compliance status records. Neo4j enables impact analysis ("if this policy changes, which compliance controls are affected?").

## 4. Storage Backend Summary

| Backend | Technology | Data Models | Use Case |
|---------|-----------|-------------|----------|
| Relational | PostgreSQL 16 | Policy, Enforcement, Assessment, Compliance | ACID transactions, referential integrity, complex queries |
| Document | MongoDB 7 | Evidence, Policy versions, Assessment reports | Flexible schema, large documents, versioned content |
| Graph | Neo4j 5 | Enforcement dependencies, Compliance mappings | Relationship traversal, impact analysis |
| Time-Series | TimescaleDB 2 | Evidence metrics | High-ingest metrics, time-based aggregation |

### 4.1 Data Flow

```
Policy defined → PostgreSQL (metadata) + MongoDB (full text)
     ↓
Evidence collected → MongoDB (documents) + TimescaleDB (metrics)
     ↓
Enforcement triggered → PostgreSQL (actions) + Neo4j (dependencies)
     ↓
Assessment conducted → PostgreSQL (findings) + MongoDB (reports)
     ↓
Compliance evaluated → PostgreSQL (status) + Neo4j (mappings)
```

### 4.2 Cross-Backend Consistency

- **UUID as universal key:** All entities use UUIDs that are consistent across backends.
- **Event-driven sync:** Changes in primary backends publish events to a message bus (Kafka/RabbitMQ) for secondary backend updates.
- **Eventual consistency:** Secondary backends (MongoDB versions, Neo4j graphs) are updated asynchronously with a maximum lag of 5 seconds.
- **Reconciliation job:** A scheduled job runs hourly to detect and repair drift between primary and secondary stores.

---

## 5. Data Retention Policies

### 5.1 Retention Classes

| Class | Duration | Applies To | Justification |
|-------|----------|------------|---------------|
| **Ephemeral** | 30 days | Debug logs, temporary scan results | Operational debugging only |
| **Standard** | 1 year | Evidence, enforcement audit logs, assessment reports | Operational and audit needs |
| **Extended** | 7 years | Compliance records, attestations, policy versions | Regulatory requirements (SOX, GDPR, etc.) |
| **Permanent** | Indefinite | Policies (active + deprecated), compliance frameworks | Organizational knowledge |

### 5.2 Retention Rules by Data Model

| Data Model | Active Records | Archived Records | Deletion |
|-----------|---------------|-----------------|----------|
| Policy | Indefinite (while active) | 7 years after deprecation | Soft delete → purge after 7 years |
| Evidence | 1 year (standard) | Move to cold storage after 1 year | Hard delete after retention class expires |
| Enforcement | Indefinite (actions) | 7 years (audit logs) | Soft delete → purge after 7 years |
| Assessment | 7 years | Move to cold storage after 7 years | Hard delete after 10 years |
| Compliance | 7 years | Permanent (attestations) | Never delete attestations; soft delete status after 7 years |

### 5.3 Retention Implementation

```sql
-- Automated partition management (PostgreSQL)
-- Monthly partitions for time-series data
CREATE TABLE evidence_metrics_2026_10 PARTITION OF evidence_metrics
    FOR VALUES FROM ('2026-10-01') TO ('2026-11-01');

-- Automated archival (pg_cron or external scheduler)
SELECT cron.schedule('0 2 * * *', $$
    -- Move records past retention to archive schema
    INSERT INTO archive.evidence_metrics
    SELECT * FROM evidence_metrics
    WHERE time < NOW() - INTERVAL '1 year';
    
    DELETE FROM evidence_metrics
    WHERE time < NOW() - INTERVAL '1 year';
$$);
```

```javascript
// MongoDB TTL index for ephemeral evidence
db.evidence.createIndex(
  { "expires_at": 1 },
  { expireAfterSeconds: 0 }
);
```

### 5.4 Legal Hold

- Any record under **legal hold** is exempt from retention policies.
- Legal hold is implemented as a `legal_hold` boolean flag + `legal_hold_reason` text field on each table.
- Records with `legal_hold = true` are never deleted, regardless of retention class.
- Legal holds require approval from the Legal team and are logged in the audit trail.

## 6. Data Encryption

### 6.1 Encryption at Rest

| Layer | Standard | Implementation |
|-------|----------|---------------|
| **Database files** | AES-256 | PostgreSQL: `pgcrypto` + filesystem encryption (LUKS/FileVault) |
| **MongoDB** | AES-256 | MongoDB Encrypted Storage Engine (WiredTiger) |
| **Neo4j** | AES-256 | Enterprise edition transparent data encryption |
| **TimescaleDB** | AES-256 | Inherits PostgreSQL encryption |
| **Backups** | AES-256 | GPG-encrypted before upload to object storage |

### 6.2 Encryption in Transit

| Connection | Standard | Implementation |
|-----------|----------|---------------|
| **App → Database** | TLS 1.3 | Mandatory for all connections |
| **Database → Database** | TLS 1.3 | Cross-backend sync connections |
| **App → Object Storage** | TLS 1.3 | S3/GCS API calls |
| **Internal service mesh** | mTLS | Istio/Linkerd between services |

### 6.3 Field-Level Encryption

Sensitive fields are encrypted at the application layer before storage:

```python
# Field-level encryption for PII and sensitive metadata
SENSITIVE_FIELDS = {
    'policies': ['metadata.owner_contact'],
    'evidence': ['content.data', 'context.metadata'],
    'enforcement': ['result', 'error_message'],
    'assessment': ['metadata.assessor_notes'],
    'compliance': ['notes', 'metadata']
}

# Encryption: AES-256-GCM with per-field keys
# Key management: AWS KMS / HashiCorp Vault
```

### 6.4 Key Management

| Aspect | Implementation |
|--------|---------------|
| **Key store** | HashiCorp Vault (primary), AWS KMS (cloud deployments) |
| **Key hierarchy** | Master key → Data encryption keys (DEKs) → Field-level keys |
| **Key rotation** | DEKs rotated every 90 days; master key rotated annually |
| **Key access** | Role-based; services authenticate via Vault tokens with TTL |
| **Key destruction** | Cryptographic erasure for data deletion requests |

### 6.5 Encryption Verification

- **Automated scan:** Weekly scan verifies all storage volumes have encryption enabled.
- **Audit log:** All encryption/decryption operations are logged with actor, timestamp, and key ID.
- **Compliance check:** Encryption status is included in compliance assessments.

## 7. Backup & Recovery

### 7.1 Backup Strategy

| Data Model | Backup Type | Frequency | Retention | Storage |
|-----------|------------|-----------|-----------|---------|
| PostgreSQL (all tables) | Full | Daily | 30 days | S3/GCS (encrypted) |
| PostgreSQL | WAL archiving | Continuous | 7 days | S3/GCS (encrypted) |
| MongoDB | Full (mongodump) | Daily | 30 days | S3/GCS (encrypted) |
| MongoDB | Oplog | Continuous | 48 hours | S3/GCS (encrypted) |
| Neo4j | Full (neo4j-admin) | Daily | 30 days | S3/GCS (encrypted) |
| TimescaleDB | Full | Daily | 30 days | S3/GCS (encrypted) |
| TimescaleDB | Continuous archiving | Real-time | 7 days | S3/GCS (encrypted) |

### 7.2 Backup Procedures

#### PostgreSQL (pgBackRest)

```bash
# Full backup
pgbackrest --stanza=grc_claw --type=full backup

# Verify backup integrity
pgbackrest --stanza=grc_claw verify

# Restore to point-in-time
pgbackrest --stanza=grc_claw \
    --type=time --target="2026-10-01 14:30:00" \
    --target-action=promote restore
```

#### MongoDB

```bash
# Full backup
mongodump --uri="mongodb://..." --archive=/backup/mongodb-$(date +%F).archive --gzip

# Point-in-time recovery
mongorestore --archive=/backup/mongodb-2026-10-01.archive --gzip \
    --oplogReplay --oplogLimit "2026-10-01T14:30:00"
```

#### Neo4j

```bash
# Full backup
neo4j-admin database backup --to-path=/backup/neo4j-$(date +%F) grc_claw

# Restore
neo4j-admin database restore --from-path=/backup/neo4j-2026-10-01 grc_claw
```

#### TimescaleDB

```bash
# Full backup (inherits pgBackRest)
pgbackrest --stanza=grc_claw_ts --type=full backup

# Continuous archiving via WAL-G
wal-g wal-push /var/lib/postgresql/wal/
```

### 7.3 Recovery Objectives

| Metric | Target | Measurement |
|--------|--------|-------------|
| **RPO (Recovery Point Objective)** | ≤ 5 minutes | Maximum data loss acceptable |
| **RTO (Recovery Time Objective)** | ≤ 4 hours | Maximum downtime acceptable |
| **RTO (critical tables)** | ≤ 1 hour | Policies, active enforcement actions |

### 7.4 Recovery Procedures

#### Scenario 1: Single Table Corruption

```sql
-- 1. Identify corruption point
-- 2. Restore table from latest good backup
pgbackrest --stanza=grc_claw --type=time \
    --target="2026-10-01 10:00:00" restore

-- 3. Replay WAL to point just before corruption
-- 4. Export affected table
-- 5. Restore to production
```

#### Scenario 2: Complete Database Loss

```bash
# 1. Provision new database instance
# 2. Restore from latest full backup
pgbackrest --stanza=grc_claw --type=full restore

# 3. Replay WAL archives to current time
pgbackrest --stanza=grc_claw --type=time \
    --target="latest" restore

# 4. Verify data integrity
psql -c "SELECT count(*) FROM policies;"
psql -c "SELECT count(*) FROM evidence;"

# 5. Rebuild secondary backends from primary
python scripts/rebuild_mongodb.py
python scripts/rebuild_neo4j.py
```

#### Scenario 3: Cross-Backend Inconsistency

```bash
# 1. Identify drift via reconciliation job
python scripts/reconcile_check.py --report

# 2. Rebuild affected secondary backend
python scripts/rebuild_neo4j.py --framework=compliance
python scripts/rebuild_mongodb.py --collection=policy_versions

# 3. Verify consistency
python scripts/reconcile_check.py --verify
```

| Backup completion | Daily | Automated alert on backup job failure |

| Restore test | Monthly | Full restore to staging environment |

### 8.1 Constraints

| **Foreign keys** | Enforced in PostgreSQL; application-level in MongoDB |

Every table includes:

```sql

updated_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
```

A separate `audit_log` table tracks all DML operations:

```sql
CREATE TABLE audit_log (

    record_id       UUID NOT NULL,
    operation       VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL,            -- INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE

    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
```

## 11. Data Lifecycle Automation

### 11.1 Lifecycle Stages

Every data record in GRC_Claw progresses through a defined lifecycle:

```
┌──────────┐    ┌──────────┐    ┌──────────┐    ┌──────────┐    ┌──────────┐
│ Ingest   │───▶│ Active   │───▶│ Warm     │───▶│ Cold     │───▶│ Purge    │
│          │    │          │    │          │    │          │    │          │
│ Validate │    │ Full CRUD│    │ Read-only│    │ Archive  │    │ Crypto   │
│ Classify │    │ Indexed  │    │ Compressed│   │ Object   │    │ Erase    │
│ Encrypt  │    │ Replicated│   │ Deduplicated│  │ Storage  │    │ or       │
│          │    │          │    │          │    │          │    │ Destroy  │
└──────────┘    └──────────┘    └──────────┘    └──────────┘    └──────────┘
```

| Stage | Duration | Storage Tier | Access Pattern | Automation |
|-------|----------|-------------|----------------|------------|
| **Ingest** | Real-time | Hot (NVMe SSD) | Write-heavy | Schema validation, classification, encryption |
| **Active** | 0–90 days | Hot (NVMe SSD) | Read + write | Full indexing, replication, backup |
| **Warm** | 90 days – 1 year | Warm (SATA SSD) | Read-occasional | Compression, deduplication, reduced indexing |
| **Cold** | 1–7 years | Cold (Object Storage) | Rare read | Archive format, minimal indexing, erasure coding |
| **Purge** | Per retention class | N/A | None | Cryptographic erasure or physical destruction |

### 11.2 Lifecycle Transition Rules

```python
class LifecycleTransitionEngine:
    """Automated lifecycle management for all GRC_Claw data."""
    
    TRANSITIONS = {
        # (current_stage, condition) -> target_stage
        ('active', 'age > 90d'): 'warm',
        ('warm', 'age > 365d'): 'cold',
        ('cold', 'retention_expired'): 'purge',
        ('active', 'legal_hold'): 'frozen',  # exempt from lifecycle
        ('warm', 'legal_hold'): 'frozen',
        ('cold', 'legal_hold'): 'frozen',
    }
    
    async def evaluate_transitions(self):
        """Run lifecycle evaluation every 6 hours."""
        for rule, target in self.TRANSITIONS.items():
            records = await self.find_matching(rule)
            for batch in self.batch(records, size=1000):
                await self.transition(batch, target)
    
    async def transition(self, records: list, target_stage: str):
        """Execute lifecycle transition with audit logging."""
        for record in records:
            # 1. Verify no legal hold
            if record.legal_hold:
                continue
            
            # 2. Apply transition actions
            if target_stage == 'warm':
                await self.compress(record)
                await self.deduplicate(record)
                await self.move_to_warm_tier(record)
            elif target_stage == 'cold':
                await self.archive_format(record)
                await self.move_to_cold_tier(record)
            elif target_stage == 'purge':
                await self.crypto_erase(record)
            
            # 3. Update metadata
            record.lifecycle_stage = target_stage
            record.stage_changed_at = datetime.utcnow()
            await self.audit_log.record_transition(record, target_stage)
```

### 11.3 Data Classification

Data is classified at ingest time to determine its lifecycle policy:

| Classification | Examples | Default Retention | Encryption | Tiering |
|---------------|----------|-------------------|------------|---------|
| **Critical** | Active policies, enforcement actions | Permanent (active) | AES-256 + field-level | Hot → Warm → Cold |
| **Operational** | Evidence, assessment reports | 1 year (standard) | AES-256 | Hot → Warm → Cold |
| **Regulatory** | Compliance records, attestations | 7 years (extended) | AES-256 + field-level | Hot → Warm → Cold |
| **Ephemeral** | Debug logs, temp scan results | 30 days | AES-256 | Hot → Purge |
| **Archival** | Deprecated policy versions | 7 years after deprecation | AES-256 | Warm → Cold |

### 11.4 Lifecycle Automation Implementation

```sql
-- PostgreSQL: Lifecycle metadata columns (added to all tables)
ALTER TABLE policies ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS lifecycle_stage VARCHAR(32) DEFAULT 'active';
ALTER TABLE policies ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS stage_changed_at TIMESTAMPTZ;
ALTER TABLE policies ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS compression_enabled BOOLEAN DEFAULT false;
ALTER TABLE policies ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS compressed_size_bytes BIGINT;
ALTER TABLE policies ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS original_size_bytes BIGINT;

-- Automated lifecycle evaluation (pg_cron)
SELECT cron.schedule('lifecycle-evaluation', '0 */6 * * *', $$
    -- Evaluate all tables for lifecycle transitions
    SELECT lifecycle_evaluate('policies');
    SELECT lifecycle_evaluate('evidence');
    SELECT lifecycle_evaluate('enforcement_actions');
    SELECT lifecycle_evaluate('assessments');
    SELECT lifecycle_evaluate('compliance_status');
$$);

-- Lifecycle evaluation function
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION lifecycle_evaluate(table_name TEXT) RETURNS INTEGER AS $$
DECLARE
    transitioned INTEGER := 0;
BEGIN
    -- Move active -> warm (age > 90 days)
    EXECUTE format(
        'UPDATE %I SET lifecycle_stage = ''warm'', stage_changed_at = NOW()
         WHERE lifecycle_stage = ''active''
         AND created_at < NOW() - INTERVAL ''90 days''
         AND (legal_hold IS NULL OR legal_hold = false)',
        table_name
    );
    GET DIAGNOSTICS transitioned = ROW_COUNT;
    
    -- Move warm -> cold (age > 365 days)
    EXECUTE format(
        'UPDATE %I SET lifecycle_stage = ''cold'', stage_changed_at = NOW()
         WHERE lifecycle_stage = ''warm''
         AND stage_changed_at < NOW() - INTERVAL ''275 days''
         AND (legal_hold IS NULL OR legal_hold = false)',
        table_name
    );
    
    RETURN transitioned;
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
```

```javascript
// MongoDB: Lifecycle metadata (added to all documents)
db.evidence.updateMany(
  { lifecycle_stage: { $exists: false } },
  { $set: { 
      lifecycle_stage: "active",
      stage_changed_at: new Date(),
      compression_enabled: false,
      original_size_bytes: 0,
      compressed_size_bytes: 0
  }}
);

// MongoDB: TTL index for ephemeral data (auto-purge)
db.evidence.createIndex(
  { "expires_at": 1 },
  { expireAfterSeconds: 0, partialFilterExpression: { retention_class: "ephemeral" } }
);

// MongoDB: Lifecycle transition (scheduled via change streams or external cron)
db.evidence.aggregate([
  { $match: { 
      lifecycle_stage: "active",
      created_at: { $lt: new Date(Date.now() - 90 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000) },
      $or: [{ legal_hold: { $exists: false } }, { legal_hold: false }]
  }},
  { $set: { lifecycle_stage: "warm", stage_changed_at: new Date() } },
  { $merge: { into: "evidence", whenMatched: "merge" }}
]);
```

### 11.5 Lifecycle Compliance & Audit

- **Transition logging:** Every lifecycle transition is recorded in the audit trail with: record ID, source stage, target stage, timestamp, triggering rule, and actor (system).
- **Retention compliance check:** Daily automated scan verifies no record exceeds its retention class duration.
- **Legal hold integration:** Records under legal hold are exempt from all automated transitions. The `lifecycle_stage` is set to `frozen` and the record is excluded from evaluation.
- **Right to erasure (GDPR Art. 17):** Data subject deletion requests trigger immediate cryptographic erasure, bypassing normal lifecycle stages. The erasure is verified and logged.
- **Lifecycle metrics:** Dashboard tracks records in each stage, transition counts, storage savings from tiering, and compliance violations.

## 12. Storage Tiering

### 12.1 Tier Definitions

GRC_Claw defines four storage tiers, each with distinct performance, cost, and durability characteristics:

| Tier | Technology | Latency (p99) | Cost/GB/Month | Durability | Use Case |
|------|-----------|---------------|---------------|------------|----------|
| **Hot** | NVMe SSD (local) | < 1 ms | $0.15–0.30 | 99.999999999% (11 nines) | Active data, enforcement path, real-time queries |
| **Warm** | SATA SSD / Cloud SSD | < 10 ms | $0.05–0.10 | 99.999999999% | Recent evidence, operational queries, analytics |
| **Cold** | Object Storage (S3/GCS) | < 500 ms | $0.01–0.03 | 99.999999999% | Archived records, compliance history, audit trail |
| **Archive** | Glacier / Coldline | < 5 seconds | $0.001–0.004 | 99.999999999% | Long-term retention, disaster recovery, legal hold |

### 12.2 Tier Assignment by Data Model

| Data Model | Hot | Warm | Cold | Archive |
|-----------|-----|------|------|---------|
| **Policies** | Active policies (0–90 days) | Deprecated policies (90d–7y) | Deprecated policies (7y+) | N/A (permanent) |
| **Evidence** | Recent evidence (0–90 days) | Standard evidence (90d–1y) | Extended evidence (1–7y) | N/A (purge after 7y) |
| **Enforcement** | Active actions (0–90 days) | Completed actions (90d–7y) | Audit logs (7y+) | N/A (purge after 7y) |
| **Assessment** | Active assessments (0–90 days) | Completed assessments (90d–7y) | Historical assessments (7–10y) | N/A (purge after 10y) |
| **Compliance** | Active status (0–90 days) | Historical status (90d–7y) | Attestations (7y+) | Attestations (permanent) |

### 12.3 Tier Transition Automation

```python
class StorageTierManager:
    """Manages data movement between storage tiers."""
    
    TIER_THRESHOLDS = {
        'hot': {'max_age_days': 90, 'storage_class': 'STANDARD'},
        'warm': {'max_age_days': 365, 'storage_class': 'STANDARD_IA'},
        'cold': {'max_age_days': 2555, 'storage_class': 'GLACIER'},  # 7 years
    }
    
    async def tier_data(self, records: list, target_tier: str):
        """Move records to target storage tier."""
        for record in records:
            # 1. Serialize to archive format
            archive_data = await self.serialize_for_tier(record, target_tier)
            
            # 2. Write to target tier
            if target_tier == 'cold':
                await self.s3_client.put_object(
                    Bucket='grc-claw-cold',
                    Key=f"{record.table_name}/{record.id}",
                    Body=archive_data,
                    StorageClass='GLACIER',
                    Metadata={
                        'original-tier': record.current_tier,
                        'transition-date': datetime.utcnow().isoformat(),
                        'retention-class': record.retention_class,
                    }
                )
            elif target_tier == 'warm':
                await self.s3_client.put_object(
                    Bucket='grc-claw-warm',
                    Key=f"{record.table_name}/{record.id}",
                    Body=archive_data,
                    StorageClass='STANDARD_IA',
                )
            
            # 3. Update metadata (keep pointer in hot tier)
            record.storage_tier = target_tier
            record.tier_transition_at = datetime.utcnow()
            record.archive_location = f"s3://grc-claw-{target_tier}/{record.table_name}/{record.id}"
            
            # 4. Delete from source tier (if moving to cold/archive)
            if target_tier in ('cold', 'archive'):
                await self.delete_from_source(record)
            
            # 5. Log transition
            await self.audit_log.record_tier_transition(record, target_tier)
```

### 12.4 Tier-Aware Query Routing

```python
class TierAwareQueryRouter:
    """Routes queries to the appropriate storage tier."""
    
    async def execute(self, query: Query) -> QueryResult:
        # 1. Determine which tiers contain relevant data
        tiers_needed = self.resolve_tiers(query)
        
        # 2. Build tier-specific queries
        results = []
        for tier in tiers_needed:
            if tier == 'hot':
                # Query PostgreSQL/MongoDB directly
                result = await self.hot_store.query(query)
            elif tier == 'warm':
                # Query warm object storage (S3 Select)
                result = await self.warm_store.query(query)
            elif tier == 'cold':
                # Query cold storage (S3 Select on Glacier Instant Retrieval)
                result = await self.cold_store.query(query)
            elif tier == 'archive':
                # Initiate Glacier retrieval job (async)
                result = await self.archive_store.initiate_retrieval(query)
            
            results.append(result)
        
        # 3. Merge and return
        return self.merge_results(results)
    
    def resolve_tiers(self, query: Query) -> list:
        """Determine which storage tiers to query based on time range."""
        tiers = ['hot']  # Always check hot
        
        if query.time_range_start < datetime.utcnow() - timedelta(days=90):
            tiers.append('warm')
        if query.time_range_start < datetime.utcnow() - timedelta(days=365):
            tiers.append('cold')
        if query.time_range_start < datetime.utcnow() - timedelta(days=2555):
            tiers.append('archive')
        
        return tiers
```

## 13. Data Compression & Deduplication

### 13.1 Compression Strategy

GRC_Claw applies compression at multiple levels to reduce storage footprint:

| Level | Algorithm | Ratio | When Applied | CPU Cost |
|-------|-----------|-------|--------------|----------|
| **Database block** | Zstandard (zstd) | 2–4x | Warm tier migration | Medium |
| **Document store** | zstd level 9 | 2–5x | Warm tier migration | Medium |
| **Object storage** | zstd level 19 | 3–6x | Cold tier archival | High (offline) |
| **Backup** | zstd level 15 | 2–4x | Backup creation | Medium |
| **Network transfer** | zstd level 3 | 2–3x | Cross-region replication | Low |

### 13.2 Compression Implementation

```python
class CompressionEngine:
    """Multi-level compression for GRC_Claw storage."""
    
    COMPRESSION_LEVELS = {
        'hot': None,  # No compression (performance)
        'warm': 'zstd:9',  # Balanced
        'cold': 'zstd:19',  # Maximum compression
        'archive': 'zstd:19',  # Maximum compression
    }
    
    async def compress_record(self, record: dict, target_tier: str) -> bytes:
        """Compress a record for the target storage tier."""
        level = self.COMPRESSION_LEVELS.get(target_tier)
        if level is None:
            return json.dumps(record).encode('utf-8')
        
        # Serialize to JSON
        raw = json.dumps(record, default=str).encode('utf-8')
        record['original_size_bytes'] = len(raw)
        
        # Compress
        compressed = zstd.compress(raw, level=int(level.split(':')[1]))
        record['compressed_size_bytes'] = len(compressed)
        record['compression_ratio'] = len(raw) / len(compressed)
        record['compression_enabled'] = True
        
        return compressed
    
    async def decompress_record(self, compressed: bytes) -> dict:
        """Decompress a record for querying."""
        raw = zstd.decompress(compressed)
        return json.loads(raw.decode('utf-8'))
```

```sql
-- PostgreSQL: Compression for large text fields
-- Use TOAST compression (automatic for large values)
ALTER TABLE policies ALTER COLUMN description SET STORAGE EXTENDED;
ALTER TABLE policy_clauses ALTER COLUMN body SET STORAGE EXTENDED;

-- Custom compression function for JSONB
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION compress_jsonb(data JSONB) RETURNS BYTEA AS $$
BEGIN
    RETURN zstd_compress(data::text::bytea, 9);
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql IMMUTABLE;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION decompress_jsonb(data BYTEA) RETURNS JSONB AS $$
BEGIN
    RETURN zstd_decompress(data)::text::jsonb;
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql IMMUTABLE;
```

### 13.3 Deduplication Strategy

Deduplication eliminates redundant data copies across the storage layer:

| Scope | Method | Savings | Implementation |
|-------|--------|---------|----------------|
| **Block-level** | Content-defined chunking (CDC) | 20–40% | Storage engine level |
| **File-level** | SHA-256 hash comparison | 10–30% | Application level |
| **Record-level** | Natural key + content hash | 5–15% | Database level |
| **Cross-tenant** | Shared policy templates | 30–50% | Reference counting |

### 13.4 Deduplication Implementation

```python
class DeduplicationEngine:
    """Content-addressable deduplication for GRC_Claw storage."""
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.chunk_size = 8192  # 8KB chunks
        self.hash_cache = LRUCache(maxsize=100000)
    
    async def deduplicate_document(self, document: dict) -> DeduplicationResult:
        """Deduplicate a document using content-defined chunking."""
        content = json.dumps(document, sort_keys=True).encode('utf-8')
        
        # 1. Check if exact duplicate exists
        content_hash = hashlib.sha256(content).hexdigest()
        existing = await self.hash_index.lookup(content_hash)
        if existing:
            return DeduplicationResult(
                is_duplicate=True,
                reference=existing,
                savings=len(content)
            )
        
        # 2. Chunk-level deduplication
        chunks = self.chunk_content(content)
        unique_chunks = []
        duplicate_chunks = []
        
        for chunk in chunks:
            chunk_hash = hashlib.sha256(chunk).hexdigest()
            cached = self.hash_cache.get(chunk_hash)
            
            if cached:
                duplicate_chunks.append(chunk_hash)
            else:
                unique_chunks.append(chunk)
                self.hash_cache[chunk_hash] = True
        
        # 3. Store unique chunks, reference duplicates
        stored_size = sum(len(c) for c in unique_chunks)
        total_size = len(content)
        
        return DeduplicationResult(
            is_duplicate=False,
            stored_size=stored_size,
            total_size=total_size,
            savings=total_size - stored_size,
            duplicate_ratio=len(duplicate_chunks) / len(chunks)
        )
    
    def chunk_content(self, content: bytes) -> list:
        """Content-defined chunking using Rabin fingerprinting."""
        chunks = []
        window_size = 48
        mask = (1 << 13) - 1  # ~8KB average chunk size
        
        i = 0
        while i < len(content):
            fingerprint = 0
            chunk_start = i
            
            for j in range(i, min(i + self.chunk_size * 2, len(content))):
                fingerprint = ((fingerprint << 1) + content[j]) & mask
                
                if fingerprint == 0 or j - chunk_start >= self.chunk_size:
                    chunks.append(content[chunk_start:j+1])
                    i = j + 1
                    break
            else:
                chunks.append(content[chunk_start:])
                i = len(content)
        
        return chunks
```

```sql
-- PostgreSQL: Deduplication hash index
CREATE TABLE dedup_hash_index (
    content_hash VARCHAR(64) PRIMARY KEY,  -- SHA-256
    reference_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
    first_seen_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    last_accessed_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    storage_location TEXT NOT NULL,  -- Where the canonical copy is stored
    size_bytes BIGINT NOT NULL
);

-- Deduplication lookup function
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION dedup_lookup(content_hash VARCHAR(64))
RETURNS TABLE(storage_location TEXT, size_bytes BIGINT) AS $$
BEGIN
    -- Update access statistics
    UPDATE dedup_hash_index
    SET last_accessed_at = NOW(),
        reference_count = reference_count + 1
    WHERE content_hash = dedup_lookup.content_hash;
    
    RETURN QUERY
    SELECT dhi.storage_location, dhi.size_bytes
    FROM dedup_hash_index dhi
    WHERE dhi.content_hash = dedup_lookup.content_hash;
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
```

### 13.5 Compression & Deduplication Metrics

| Metric | Target | Measurement |
|--------|--------|-------------|
| Compression ratio (warm) | ≥ 3:1 | Compressed size / Original size |
| Compression ratio (cold) | ≥ 5:1 | Compressed size / Original size |
| Deduplication ratio | ≥ 20% | Duplicate bytes / Total bytes |
| Storage savings | ≥ 40% | (Original - Actual) / Original |
| Decompression latency | < 50ms | p99 for single record |
| Compression CPU overhead | < 10% | CPU time / Total processing time |

## 14. Storage Performance Optimization

### 14.1 Indexing Strategy

```sql
-- PostgreSQL: Performance indexes for common query patterns

-- Composite indexes for enforcement queries
CREATE INDEX idx_enforcement_active ON enforcement_actions(policy_id, status, priority)
    WHERE status IN ('pending', 'in_progress');

-- Partial indexes for active records (hot data)
CREATE INDEX idx_policies_active ON policies(category, status)
    WHERE status = 'active';

-- BRIN indexes for time-series data (space-efficient)
CREATE INDEX idx_evidence_metrics_time ON evidence_metrics USING BRIN(time)
    WITH (pages_per_range = 32);

-- GIN indexes for JSONB metadata queries
CREATE INDEX idx_policies_metadata ON policies USING GIN(metadata jsonb_path_ops);
CREATE INDEX idx_enforcement_result ON enforcement_actions USING GIN(result jsonb_path_ops);

-- Covering indexes for common lookups
CREATE INDEX idx_compliance_status_lookup ON compliance_status(framework_id, control_id, target_type, target_id)
    INCLUDE (status, evaluated_at, next_review_at);
```

```javascript
// MongoDB: Performance indexes
// Compound index for evidence queries
db.evidence.createIndex({ "policy_id": 1, "validation.status": 1, "created_at": -1 });

// Text index for evidence content search
db.evidence.createIndex({ "content.data": "text", "source.system": "text" });

// Hashed index for even distribution
db.evidence.createIndex({ "evidence_id": "hashed" });

// Partial index for active evidence only
db.evidence.createIndex(
  { "created_at": -1 },
  { partialFilterExpression: { "validation.status": "pending" } }
);
```

### 14.2 Query Optimization

```python
class QueryOptimizer:
    """Storage query optimization for GRC_Claw."""
    
    async def optimize_query(self, query: Query) -> OptimizedQuery:
        """Apply storage-level query optimizations."""
        
        # 1. Partition pruning
        partitions = self.prune_partitions(query)
        
        # 2. Index selection
        plan = self.select_index(query, partitions)
        
        # 3. Query rewriting
        rewritten = self.rewrite_query(query, plan)
        
        # 4. Parallel execution strategy
        execution_plan = self.create_execution_plan(rewritten, partitions)
        
        return OptimizedQuery(
            sql=execution_plan.sql,
            params=execution_plan.params,
            partitions=partitions,
            estimated_cost=execution_plan.cost,
            cache_hint=execution_plan.cache_hint
        )
    
    def prune_partitions(self, query: Query) -> list:
        """Eliminate partitions that cannot contain relevant data."""
        if query.time_range:
            # Only query partitions that overlap with time range
            return [
                p for p in self.partitions
                if p.time_range.overlaps(query.time_range)
            ]
        return self.partitions
    
    def rewrite_query(self, query: Query, plan: IndexPlan) -> str:
        """Rewrite query for optimal execution."""
        # Convert OR to UNION for better index usage
        if query.has_or_conditions:
            return self.or_to_union(query)
        
        # Add covering index hints
        if plan.covering_index:
            return f"/*+ INDEX({plan.covering_index}) */ {query.sql}"
        
        return query.sql
```

### 14.5 Performance Monitoring

```sql
-- PostgreSQL: Performance monitoring views
CREATE VIEW v_storage_performance AS
SELECT
    schemaname,
    relname AS table_name,
    seq_scan,
    idx_scan,
    n_tup_ins,
    n_tup_upd,
    n_tup_del,
    n_live_tup,
    n_dead_tup,
    last_vacuum,
    last_autovacuum,
    last_analyze,
    last_autoanalyze,
    pg_total_relation_size(relid) AS total_size_bytes,
    pg_relation_size(relid) AS table_size_bytes,
    pg_indexes_size(relid) AS index_size_bytes
FROM pg_stat_user_tables
JOIN pg_class ON relname = relname
ORDER BY pg_total_relation_size(relid) DESC;

-- Alert on table bloat
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION check_table_bloat() RETURNS TABLE(table_name TEXT, bloat_ratio NUMERIC) AS $$
BEGIN
    RETURN QUERY
    SELECT
        relname,
        n_dead_tup::numeric / NULLIF(n_live_tup, 0) AS bloat_ratio
    FROM pg_stat_user_tables
    WHERE n_dead_tup > 10000
    AND n_dead_tup::numeric / NULLIF(n_live_tup, 0) > 0.2;
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
```

## 15. Multi-Region Replication

### 15.1 Replication Architecture

GRC_Claw supports multi-region replication for disaster recovery, data residency, and low-latency global access:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        Multi-Region Replication                          │
│                                                                         │
│  ┌─────────────────┐         ┌─────────────────┐         ┌─────────────┐│
│  │  us-east-1      │         │  eu-west-1      │         │ ap-south-1  ││
│  │  (Primary)      │         │  (Replica)      │         │ (Replica)   ││
│  │                 │         │                 │         │             ││
│  │  PostgreSQL     │◄────────│  PostgreSQL     │◄────────│ PostgreSQL  ││
│  │  (Patroni HA)   │  Sync    │  (Patroni HA)   │  Async   │ (Patroni HA)││
│  │                 │         │                 │         │             ││
│  │  MongoDB        │◄────────│  MongoDB        │◄────────│ MongoDB     ││
│  │  (Replica Set)  │  Async   │  (Replica Set)  │  Async   │ (Replica Set)│
│  │                 │         │                 │         │             ││
│  │  Neo4j          │◄────────│  Neo4j          │         │ Neo4j       ││
│  │  (Causal Cluster)│  Async  │  (Causal Cluster)│  N/A    │ (Causal Cl.)││
│  │                 │         │                 │         │             ││
│  │  TimescaleDB    │◄────────│  TimescaleDB    │         │ TimescaleDB ││
│  │  (Streaming)    │  Async   │  (Streaming)    │  N/A    │ (Streaming) ││
│  │                 │         │                 │         │             ││
│  │  S3 (Primary)   │────────►│  S3 (Replica)   │────────►│ S3 (Replica)││
│  │  (CRR)          │         │  (CRR)          │         │ (CRR)       ││
│  └─────────────────┘         └─────────────────┘         └─────────────┘│
│                                                                         │
│  Replication modes:                                                    │
│  • PostgreSQL: Synchronous (same region) + Async (cross-region)        │
│  • MongoDB: Asynchronous replica sets (cross-region)                   │
│  • Neo4j: Causal clustering (same region) + read replicas (cross-region)│
│  • TimescaleDB: Streaming replication (same region)                    │
│  • S3: Cross-region replication (CRR)                                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### 15.2 Replication Modes

| Backend | Same-Region | Cross-Region | Consistency | RPO |
|---------|-------------|--------------|-------------|-----|
| **PostgreSQL** | Synchronous (Patroni) | Asynchronous (logical replication) | Strong (same region) / Eventual (cross-region) | < 1s (same) / < 30s (cross) |
| **MongoDB** | Replica set (majority) | Replica set (async) | Eventual | < 10s |
| **Neo4j** | Causal cluster (Raft) | Read replicas | Causal (same) / Eventual (cross) | < 5s (same) / < 60s (cross) |
| **TimescaleDB** | Streaming replication | N/A (single region) | Strong | < 1s |
| **S3** | N/A | Cross-region replication (CRR) | Eventual | < 15 min |

### 15.3 Cross-Region Replication Configuration

```yaml
# PostgreSQL: Cross-region logical replication
# Primary region (us-east-1)
publication:
  name: grc_claw_publication
  tables:
    - policies
    - policy_clauses
    - enforcement_actions
    - assessments
    - compliance_status

# Replica region (eu-west-1)
subscription:
  name: grc_claw_eu_subscription
  connection: "host=grc-claw-us-east-1.db.internal port=5432 dbname=grc_claw"
  publication: grc_claw_publication
  copy_data: true
  create_slot: true
  enabled: true
  slot_name: grc_claw_eu_slot
  commit_delay: 0  # No delay for compliance data

---
# MongoDB: Cross-region replica set
replication:
  replSetName: grc-claw-rs
  members:
    - _id: 0
      host: mongo-0.us-east-1:27017
      priority: 5  # Primary
    - _id: 1
      host: mongo-1.us-east-1:27017
      priority: 3  # Secondary
    - _id: 2
      host: mongo-2.eu-west-1:27017
      priority: 1  # Cross-region secondary
      votes: 1
    - _id: 3
      host: mongo-3.eu-west-1:27017
      priority: 0  # Arbiter (no data)
      arbiterOnly: true

---

  Role: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/grc-claw-replication
  Rules:
    - Id: ReplicateToEU
      Status: Enabled
      Priority: 1
      DeleteMarkerReplication:
        Status: Enabled
      Destination:
        Bucket: arn:aws:s3:::grc-claw-eu-west-1
        StorageClass: STANDARD
        ReplicationTime:
          Status: Enabled
          Time:
            Minutes: 15
        Metrics:
          Status: Enabled
          EventThreshold:
            Minutes: 15
      Filter:
        Prefix: ""  # Replicate all objects
```

### 15.4 Data Residency Enforcement

```python
class DataResidencyEnforcer:
    """Enforces data residency requirements for multi-region deployments."""
    
    RESIDENCY_RULES = {
        'EU': {
            'allowed_regions': ['eu-west-1', 'eu-central-1'],
            'storage_class': 'STANDARD',
            'encryption_key': 'arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:123456789:key/eu-key',
            'replication': 'intra-region-only',
        },
        'US': {
            'allowed_regions': ['us-east-1', 'us-west-2'],
            'storage_class': 'STANDARD',
            'encryption_key': 'arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789:key/us-key',
            'replication': 'cross-region-allowed',
        },
        'CN': {
            'allowed_regions': ['cn-north-1', 'cn-northwest-1'],
            'storage_class': 'STANDARD',
            'encryption_key': 'arn:aws:kms:cn-north-1:123456789:key/cn-key',
            'replication': 'intra-region-only',
        },
    }
    
    async def enforce_residency(self, tenant_id: str, data: dict):
        """Ensure data is stored in compliance with residency rules."""
        tenant = await self.tenant_registry.get(tenant_id)
        residency = tenant.data_residency
        
        rules = self.RESIDENCY_RULES.get(residency)
        if not rules:
            raise ResidencyError(f"No residency rules for {residency}")
        
        # 1. Verify write is to allowed region
        current_region = self.get_current_region()
        if current_region not in rules['allowed_regions']:
            raise ResidencyError(
                f"Data for tenant {tenant_id} must be in {residency}, "
                f"not {current_region}"
            )
        
        # 2. Apply region-specific encryption
        data['encryption_key_id'] = rules['encryption_key']
        
        # 3. Configure replication
        if rules['replication'] == 'intra-region-only':
            data['replication_policy'] = 'none'
        else:
            data['replication_policy'] = 'cross-region'
        
        return data
```

### 15.5 Replication Monitoring & Failover

```python
class ReplicationMonitor:
    """Monitors replication health and manages failover."""
    
    async def check_replication_health(self) -> ReplicationHealth:
        """Check replication status across all regions."""
        health = ReplicationHealth()
        
        for region in self.regions:
            # Check PostgreSQL replication lag
            pg_lag = await self.get_postgresql_lag(region)
            health.postgresql_lag[region] = pg_lag
            
            # Check MongoDB replication lag
            mongo_lag = await self.get_mongodb_lag(region)
            health.mongodb_lag[region] = mongo_lag
            
            # Check S3 replication status
            s3_status = await self.get_s3_replication_status(region)
            health.s3_replication[region] = s3_status
            
            # Alert if lag exceeds thresholds
            if pg_lag > 30:
                self.alert(f"PostgreSQL replication lag in {region}: {pg_lag}s")
            if mongo_lag > 60:
                self.alert(f"MongoDB replication lag in {region}: {mongo_lag}s")
        
        return health
    
    async def initiate_failover(self, failed_region: str):
        """Initiate cross-region failover."""
        # 1. Promote replica in target region
        target_region = self.select_failover_target(failed_region)
        
        # 2. Update DNS/routing
        await self.gslb.update_routing(failed_region, target_region)
        
        # 3. Promote PostgreSQL replica
        await self.patroni.promote(target_region)
        
        # 4. Promote MongoDB replica
        await self.mongodb.step_up(target_region)
        
        # 5. Update application configuration
        await self.config.update_primary_region(target_region)
        
        # 6. Notify stakeholders
        self.notify(f"Failover from {failed_region} to {target_region} complete")
```

## 16. Storage Cost Optimization

### 16.1 Cost Model

| Cost Component | Tier 1 | Tier 2 | Tier 3 | Tier 4 |
|---------------|--------|--------|--------|--------|
| **Hot storage** | $50/mo | $500/mo | $5,000/mo | $50,000/mo |
| **Warm storage** | $10/mo | $100/mo | $1,000/mo | $10,000/mo |
| **Cold storage** | $5/mo | $50/mo | $500/mo | $5,000/mo |
| **Archive** | $1/mo | $10/mo | $100/mo | $1,000/mo |
| **Data transfer** | $10/mo | $100/mo | $1,000/mo | $10,000/mo |
| **Backup storage** | $20/mo | $200/mo | $2,000/mo | $20,000/mo |
| **Total estimated** | **$96/mo** | **$960/mo** | **$9,600/mo** | **$96,000/mo** |

### 16.2 Cost Optimization Strategies

| Strategy | Implementation | Savings | Effort |
|----------|---------------|---------|--------|
| **Storage tiering** | Auto-move cold data to object storage | 70–90% | Low |
| **Compression** | zstd compression on warm/cold data | 40–60% | Low |
| **Deduplication** | Content-addressable deduplication | 20–40% | Medium |
| **Right-sizing** | Continuous resource utilization analysis | 20–30% | Medium |
| **Reserved capacity** | 1-year commit for baseline capacity | 30–50% | Low |
| **Spot instances** | Spot for evidence collectors and analytics | 60–90% | Low |
| **Scale-to-zero** | Non-production environments scale to zero | 50–80% | Low |
| **Lifecycle automation** | Automated data purging per retention | 10–20% | Low |

### 16.3 Cost Monitoring & Alerting

```python
class StorageCostMonitor:
    """Monitors and optimizes storage costs across all tiers."""
    
    async def generate_cost_report(self) -> CostReport:
        """Generate daily storage cost report."""
        report = CostReport(date=datetime.utcnow().date())
        
        for region in self.regions:
            # Get storage usage by tier
            usage = await self.get_storage_usage(region)
            
            # Calculate costs
            for tier, size_gb in usage.items():
                cost = size_gb * self.TIER_RATES[tier]
                report.add_line_item(
                    region=region,
                    tier=tier,
                    size_gb=size_gb,
                    cost=cost
                )
            
            # Identify optimization opportunities
            opportunities = self.identify_optimizations(region, usage)
            report.add_opportunities(opportunities)
        
        return report
    
    def identify_optimizations(self, region: str, usage: dict) -> list:
        """Identify cost optimization opportunities."""
        opportunities = []
        
        # 1. Data in hot tier that should be warm
        hot_data_age = self.get_hot_data_age(region)
        if hot_data_age['p95'] > 90:
            opportunities.append({
                'type': 'tier_transition',
                'description': f"Move {hot_data_age['size_gb']} GB from hot to warm",
                'savings': hot_data_age['size_gb'] * (self.TIER_RATES['hot'] - self.TIER_RATES['warm']),
                'effort': 'low',
            })
        
        # 2. Uncompressed data in warm/cold tier
        uncompressed = self.get_uncompressed_data(region)
        if uncompressed > 0:
            opportunities.append({
                'type': 'compression',
                'description': f"Compress {uncompressed} GB of uncompressed data",
                'savings': uncompressed * 0.5 * self.TIER_RATES['warm'],  # ~50% reduction
                'effort': 'low',
            })
        
        # 3. Duplicate data
        duplicates = self.get_duplicate_data(region)
        if duplicates > 0:
            opportunities.append({
                'type': 'deduplication',
                'description': f"Deduplicate {duplicates} GB of redundant data",
                'savings': duplicates * self.TIER_RATES['warm'],
                'effort': 'medium',
            })
        
        # 4. Over-provisioned resources
        over_provisioned = self.get_over_provisioned_resources(region)
        if over_provisioned:
            opportunities.append({
                'type': 'right_sizing',
                'description': f"Right-size {over_provisioned['count']} over-provisioned resources",
                'savings': over_provisioned['monthly_cost'] * 0.3,  # ~30% savings
                'effort': 'medium',
            })
        
        return opportunities
```

### 16.4 Storage Cost Allocation

```sql
-- PostgreSQL: Storage cost allocation by tenant
CREATE VIEW v_storage_cost_by_tenant AS
SELECT
    tenant_id,
    'hot' AS tier,
    pg_total_relation_size(relid) / 1024.0 / 1024.0 / 1024.0 AS size_gb,
    pg_total_relation_size(relid) / 1024.0 / 1024.0 / 1024.0 * 0.15 AS monthly_cost
FROM pg_stat_user_tables
JOIN pg_class ON relname = relname
WHERE schemaname = 'tenant_' || tenant_id::text

UNION ALL

SELECT
    tenant_id,
    'warm' AS tier,
    SUM(size_bytes) / 1024.0 / 1024.0 / 1024.0 AS size_gb,
    SUM(size_bytes) / 1024.0 / 1024.0 / 1024.0 * 0.05 AS monthly_cost
FROM warm_storage_objects
GROUP BY tenant_id

UNION ALL

SELECT
    tenant_id,
    'cold' AS tier,
    SUM(size_bytes) / 1024.0 / 1024.0 / 1024.0 AS size_gb,
    SUM(size_bytes) / 1024.0 / 1024.0 / 1024.0 * 0.01 AS monthly_cost
FROM cold_storage_objects
GROUP BY tenant_id;
```
